item.title: Black Friday hype stems from a desire 'to be part of a collective event', expert says
item.description: Once a strictly US affair, it's become a truly global phenomenon. From shoppers hunting for bargains in Louisiana, to queues forming outside stores in Venezuela, the Black Friday sales event has become the biggest day of the year for retail foot traffic. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Olaya Moldes Andres, Associate Professor in Marketing and Strategy at Cardiff Business School. She explains that, beyond the sales, the success of Black Friday may also be due to a desire by shoppers to "join the collective action. Whether it is spending money or going to the mall, shoppers feel part of a collective event, so perhaps this is where the whole hype comes from, to feel that we're being part of something, same thing as Christmas or any other social event".

item.description: FIFA has confirmed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will host the 2031 Women's World Cup — the first to feature 48 teams. The UK will stage the 2035 edition, its first World Cup since 1966.

item.title: Gukesh to defend chess crown against rising star Sindarov
item.description: As the World Chess championship gets underway, it's no coincidence that the titleholder, Gukesh Dommaraju, and his challenger, Jakhovir Sindarov, are both from Asia.

item.title: Nvidia reinstates former CEO Jensen Huang despite China espionage scandal
item.description: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to bring back the disgraced CEO, who resigned this month amid news of his affairs. He's suspected of having had a relationship with a Chinese intelligence asset.

item.title: North Macedonia remains stalled on its EU path after 21 years as a candidate
item.description: EU enlargement has regained momentum, with Montenegro and Albania moving closer to membership. But North Macedonia, a candidate since 2005, remains stalled by a politically difficult dispute involving Bulgaria.

item.title: Uganda minister at COP31: 'We need a just transition'
item.description: Funding from wealthy countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change hasn't materialized, says Uganda's environment minister. The East African country is hoping oil and carbon credits will help boost finances.

item.title: COP deadlock prompts calls for a reset of climate diplomacy
item.description: COP31 has been branded a failure after countries couldn't reach a final agreement, divided over a reference to "fossil fuels." But was the decision to walk away from a watered-down text actually a show of strength?

item.title: German police respond to multiple school bomb threats
item.description: Police in Germany are responding to bomb threats against a series of schools, but say that at present they don't believe them to be credible. Danish authorities are reporting a similar series of apparent hoaxes.

item.title: 'I've lost her forever' — Why German voice actors are refusing to sign Netflix's AI contract
item.description: For decades, Germans have known Hollywood's biggest stars through the same familiar voices. Now an AI clause in Netflix contracts is splitting the industry over whether it protects performers or exposes them.

item.title: Budget cuts threaten Germany's fight against antisemitism and racism
item.description: Numerous grassroots initiatives in Germany are facing funding cuts. Affected organizations are sounding the alarm, pointing to growing challenges posed by far-right extremism.

item.title: Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' is more alive than you'd expect
item.description: A new project and exhibition, "The Night Watch Lives," lifts the veil on the hidden world of microbes covering one of the most famous paintings of the Dutch Golden Age.

item.title: Germany's Early Start Pension: Can child investment accounts help?
item.description: Germany plans to pay €10 a month into investment accounts for children to encourage long-term retirement saving. Economists say the measure may help build wealth but won't solve the country's pension funding challenge.

item.title: Germany news: Metalworkers go on strike as pay dispute heats up
item.description: Germany's biggest union is calling for more strikes over heated pay disputes with car makers like Mercedes and shipyards among the companies impacted. Meanwhile, a Berlin hospital fire leaves many injured.

item.title: Rule-breaking is contagious — and good examples barely help
item.description: Seeing someone break a rule makes people more likely to break it too, a new study has found, especially when the rule-breaker is on their side politically. Watching others behave well barely made a difference.

item.title: COP31 climate talks end without consensus on how to fund vulnerable countries or move the world away from coal, oil and gas use
item.description: After two weeks of tough talks, the COP31 climate summit has closed without a consensus on how to quit fossil fuels or fund countries struggling to adapt to a hotter world.

item.title: Inspired by Bernie Sanders: A German agency is using US-Style campaigning to boost the left in 2029
item.description: "The Goodforces" wants to see a swing to the left in the 2029 German elections. The agency counts New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Bernie Sanders among its inspirations. Could it transform the political landscape?

item.title: Germany news: IG Metall union calls for new 24-hour strike
item.description: Germany's biggest single union, IG Metall, is calling on car and shipyard workers to strike amid a pay row. Meanwhile, Germany's president is setting off on an Africa trip. DW has more.

item.title: Russian helicopter suspected of violating Finnish airspace
item.description: Finland's Defense Ministry thinks the incursion is linked to a drone strike earlier Saturday on a Russian cargo ship, which is on a US sanctions list.

item.title: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal
item.description: A deal covering 730 million people promises lower tariffs and new investment opportunities as the European Union seeks to diversify trade ties amid growing global economic tensions.

item.title: EU takes aim at tech giants in tax proposal
item.description: European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a smaller EU budget for 2028-2034, including a 3% tax on major digital firms to ease member states' contributions. France has already rejected the plan as inadequate.

item.title: Russia strikes Zelenskyy's hometown, killing 2
item.description: The attacks follow Russian President Vladimir Putin's vow of a "painful" response to Ukraine's attacks this week on the Kerch Bridge, linking Russian-occupied Crimea.

item.title: Germany's religious freedom report: Authoritarian regimes, holy wars, and spies abroad
item.description: Harassment, persecution, surveillance: Across much of the world, people of faith are facing growing pressure. A new German government report is unusually direct in criticizing China in particular.

item.title: Russian ornithologist jailed over small donations to Navalny's foundation
item.description: Sofia Rosenfeld has devoted her life to studying Arctic birds. A Russian court sentenced her to 3.5 years in a penal colony over donations to Navalny's foundation. Friends and family are fighting for her release.

item.title: COP31: No agreement on climate science, disinformation spreading
item.description: Attacks on climate science and disinformation risk delaying key measures at COP31 in Antalya. As the UN climate talks draw to a close, how will that affect efforts to come to an agreement?

item.title: Has the 'Parthenon puzzle' been solved? The long quest to reassemble lost eastern pediment
item.description: The depiction of the birth of the goddess Athena above the Parthenon's entrance is considered a masterpiece of ancient art. Now, a German research team has pieced together all the surviving fragments.

item.title: Better educated than ever — yet Germany's Gen Z is being shut out of its own future
item.description: Never before have young people around the world been so well-educated while facing so many economic challenges. Young Germans are asking: Will I be better off than my parents?

item.title: Measles in America: Here's a constructive approach to beating the disease, based on Brazil's experience
item.description: The US is now officially a measles contagion zone. By mid-2026, there were more infections than in all of the previous year. But the country could beat measles again, just like Brazil did two years ago.

item.title: Germany face Belgium in Nations League quarterfinals — Klopp plays down favorites tag
item.description: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is looking to "carry positive momentum forward" as his team draw neighboring Belgium in the quarterfinals of the UEFA Nations League.

item.title: EU and UK strike 'landmark deal' to strengthen ties after Brexit
item.description: The European Union and the United Kingdom have agreed on "landmark" deals on youth mobility and trade. Leaders on both sides praised the agreement as they seek to rebuild ties.

item.title: Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
item.description: In the latest in a series of raids and arrests, another major pro-opposition Turkish broadcaster has been brought under state control. This is the third in a year.

item.title: FIFA presidential election 2027: Infantino facing Diallo and Tashima — could an alliance change everything?
item.description: Two challengers to Gianni Infantino have registered for next year's FIFA presidential election. What do Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima stand for – and do they stand a chance against the incumbent?

item.title: Lufthansa to cut 1,000 jobs, citing ongoing losses — reports
item.description: According to a letter obtained by the media, Lufthansa's executive board said the German company is losing €20 million every month. In addition to job cuts, operational cuts are also planned.

item.title: Have we missed our chance to stop climate change?
item.description: From record-breaking heat to devastating floods and wildfires, the warning signs are everywhere. Can rising temperatures still be brought under control?

item.title: Putin proposes second humanitarian ceasefire — is it a trap?
item.description: Russian President Putin has suggested evacuating civilians from the embattled Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka. But experts warn this could serve military, not humanitarian, aims. What should Kyiv do?

item.title: No mention of fossil fuels in latest COP31 draft deal
item.description: One of the most fraught debates at the UN climate talks in Turkey has revolved around the future of coal, oil and gas. Now, all mention of fossil fuels has been removed from the summit's new draft agreement.

item.title: Anthropic trading tests investors' appetite for AI
item.description: Anthropic was valued at $2 trillion after shares started trading on the Nasdaq following a record $81 billion IPO. Its performance will put investor confidence in AI to the test.

item.title: Alexander Zverev faces fresh lawsuit from ex-girlfriend
item.description: World No. 1 tennis player Alexander Zverev is facing a new lawsuit related to a domestic abuse trial. The lawyer for his ex-girlfriend, Brenda Patea, told DW what the allegations are against the German player.

item.title: EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack using AI tools
item.description: The European Commission was targeted by an "AI-generated cybercampaign," a spokesperson has said. This is the first time the bloc has publicly reported an AI-based cyberattack.

item.title: Wadephul: 'Coalition of the Willing' talks in Berlin send strong signal to Moscow
item.description: German Foreign Minister Wadephul has said the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin sends a clear message to Moscow to take peace talks seriously. He also warned Ukraine should be prepared for peace talks to fail.

item.title: Iran balances ties with China and Russia as Trump ramps up pressure
item.description: As Donald Trump seeks to tighten economic pressure on Iran, China remains its biggest oil customer and Russia a key partner. But both powers are balancing support for Tehran against broader interests with Washington.

item.title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
item.description: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms and the Nvidia scandal has cast doubt on Anthropic's IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.

item.title: Borussia Dortmund bows to fan pressure and end Rheinmetall deal
item.description: Borussia Dortmund has reluctantly ended its association with a major sponsor after long-term fan protests. They are not the first Bundesliga club to u-turn, as commercial interests clash with politics and fan culture.

item.title: 'Coalition of the Willing' meets in Berlin: Europe remains committed to Ukraine
item.description: The "Coalition of the Willing" supporting Ukraine is gathering in Berlin. One of the key issues under discussion is whether Europe will be able to play a role in future negotiations over the country's future.

item.title: How a green economy could help reverse climate change
item.description: Green growth promises a future in which economies thrive without destroying the environment. But is this vision realistic?

item.title: Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers
item.description: Former President Hashim Thaci has been convicted of trying to influence witnesses in his war crimes trial. The conviction has reignited debate in Kosovo about the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, the court that convicted him.

item.title: Back to 1997: Russia wants NATO to roll back its eastern expansion
item.description: The Kremlin is reportedly calling on NATO to withdraw from large parts of Eastern Europe. What this would mean for the security of millions of Europeans — and what lies behind Russia's plan.

item.title: Rights court rules Turkey must release jailed lawmaker Atalay
item.description: The European Court of Human Rights has called for the release of imprisoned elected lawmaker Can Atalay. Atalay has been in prison for almost five years despite rulings from the Turkish Constitutional Court.

item.title: Nvidia forms national security committee after Huang affair
item.description: Nvidia has created a board-level committee for national security and export control. This follows the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang over extramarital affairs, allegedly including one with a Chinese intelligence asset.

item.title: Students' List candidates take seats as Serbian parliament opens
item.description: Serbia's Student List's candidates have taken their oaths in the inaugural parliament session. As the new majority, they have 90 days to form a government.

item.title: Klopp and Wirtz offer glimpse of bright German future
item.description: Germany's fall from grace in recent years has seen the team drift away from the fans. But Monday's drubbing of the Netherlands and the impact of Jürgen Klopp, Florian Wirtz and emerging youngsters offers hope.

item.title: Could the Airbus €3 billion loan row reignite a US-EU trade dispute?
item.description: The US says a record €3 billion financing package for Airbus may conflict with a transatlantic aircraft-subsidy truce. EU officials insist the funding complies with market-based rules.

item.title: Germany news: Plans for Rwanda migrant hub come under fire
item.description: Human rights groups have slammed plans by Germany and four other EU states to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda. In other news, business start-ups in Germany are on track to reach the highest level since 2015.

item.title: France's Philippe Diallo to challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency
item.description: Philippe Diallo is the second candidate to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino. He is backed by European football's governing body UEFA, known to be critical of Infantino.

item.title: NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away from Earth
item.description: When just saying 'hello' takes a two-day round trip, you're a light-day, or 26 billion kilometers, from Earth. Only one human-made object has ever traveled that far — and its journey into interstellar space continues.

item.title: What has changed in James Bond films over the decades
item.description: In 1962, a martini-drinking womanizer saved the world for the first time in "Dr. No." As Robert Pattinson takes on the role of 007, here's how the films evolved.

item.title: The AfD and neo-Nazi networks: How close are the connections?
item.description: The Alternative for Germany party (AfD) has become a focal point for the far right. Many of its members and staff have ties to ethnonationalist or neo-Nazi organizations.

item.title: COP31 draft deal calls for 'immediate' shift away from fossil fuels
item.description: The preliminary agreement at UN climate talks in Turkey calls for a rapid reduction of planet-warming emissions and at least $120 billion to help countries adapt to climate change.

item.title: Klopp wants Infantino out as FIFA candidate deadline looms
item.description: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has joined the chorus of football figures critical of FIFA President Gianni Infantino. But with time running out, there are few who seem willing to run against him.

item.title: Germany news: Merz, Söder aim to revisit electricity tax cut
item.description: The Christian Democrats are in Munich, pushing to revive some tax relief that didn't make it into the budget after talks last week. And Manuela Schwesig faces a vote on a new term as regional leader. Follow DW.

item.title: Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?
item.description: In April, about 60 countries held an unprecedented meeting in Colombia to work out a plan to slowly quit oil, coal and gas. How influential is this coalition at the COP31 climate summit?

item.title: AI in classrooms: Fighting the great 'dumbing down'
item.description: Research suggests that students who aren't careful about how they use ChatGPT and other AI tools risk poorer academic outcomes. It's a huge challenge for teachers.
